evidence: Measured in 1 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.14% of total volatiles (0.028mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Caryophyllenyl alcohol is a botanical compound known as a sesquiterpene alcohol, closely related to the spicy, woody terpene caryophyllene. People most often encounter it as a trace component in the aromatic essential oils of certain plants and herbs.
consumer_summary.found_in: It has been identified in the essential oils of hemp and in extracts of the wild herb Sonchus asper.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to caryophyllenyl alcohol to understand how it contributes to the defensive properties of the plants that produce it. Early laboratory work (Oxford level 5, in vitro) is exploring its potential to help fight off unwanted bacteria. If this bears out, it could help explain the traditional uses of the plants it comes from and inspire new botanical formulations.

structure_function.statement: Early laboratory work points toward a potential role in supporting the body's natural defenses against certain microbes.
structure_function.basis: This rests on a single in vitro study examining the antimicrobial activity of plant extracts containing the compound.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether caryophyllenyl alcohol contributes to the bacteria-fighting power of hemp essential oils and other plant extracts. If this bears out, it could be isolated or concentrated for use in natural topical botanical defenses.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: An animal model of topical bacterial infection comparing a standardized dose of isolated caryophyllenyl alcohol against a vehicle control over 7 to 14 days to measure bacterial load reduction.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: The best evidence so far is early laboratory research (Oxford level 5); no human or animal trials have been published yet.
